Paper: Qin et al., "How Different are the Cloud Workloads? Characterizing Large-Scale Private and Public Cloud Workloads", IEEE/IFIP DSN 2023
Method: Empirical characterisation of private vs public fleets
Dataset / Testbed: Microsoft private cloud + Azure public cloud traces
Metric: Utilisation distributions, deployment size, burst frequency
Limitation: Descriptive only; proposes no sizing policy, so violation exposure is never quantified

Paper: Towards Workload-aware Cloud Efficiency: A Large-scale Empirical Study of Cloud Workload Characteristics, ACM 2025
Method: Large-scale empirical study of workload characteristics vs cloud efficiency
Limitation: Quantifies waste at fleet scale but does not prescribe reclamation, so never confronts induced risk

Paper: Coach: Exploiting Temporal Patterns for All-Resource Oversubscription in Cloud Platforms, arXiv:2501.11179, 2025 [preprint]
Method: Temporal pattern exploitation for CPU and memory oversubscription
Limitation: Host-level pooling rather than per-VM shrinking; risk absorbed by platform, not exposed to the operator

Paper: Majd, Cheng, Pahlevan, Meinel, "Right-sizing Recommendations (RSR): Cloud Workload Conformal Prediction for VMs in Data Center Operations", IEEE/WIC WI-IAT 2025
Method: Bootstrapping conformal prediction over ML regressions; model ranking by backtesting
Metric: Forecast error, prediction-interval coverage and width
Limitation: Reports interval coverage instead of consequence; recommendations never replayed against held-out demand, so exhaustion events go uncounted

Paper: CLOUDADV: Decision-Aligned Instance Sizing with Zero-Shot Foundation Models under Drift, arXiv:2606.31470, 2026 [preprint]
Method: Zero-shot time-series foundation model for instance sizing under drift
Metric: Sizing decision quality, cost savings under drift
Limitation: Delivers a single operating point with no risk axis; operator cannot choose exposure

Paper: Kollu et al., "Comparative analysis of cloud resources forecasting using deep learning techniques based on VM workload traces", Trans. Emerging Telecommunications Technologies 35(1):e4933, 2024
Method: Comparative MLP / ARNN / CNN / LSTM forecasting of CPU and memory
Limitation: Accuracy is the terminal metric; no allocation is set from the forecast and no exhaustion event is counted

Paper: Pan et al., "MagicScaler: Uncertainty-aware, Predictive Autoscaling", PVLDB 16(12):3808-3821, 2023
Method: Multi-scale attentive Gaussian process predictor + uncertainty-aware scaler with stochastic-constraint loss
Dataset / Testbed: Alibaba Cloud ECS production traces, three clusters
Metric: Cost vs QoS violation risk trade-off
Limitation: Risk is a loss-function constraint, not a reported probability; trade-off drawn against cost not reclaimed capacity; calibration never validated

Paper: Zou et al., "OptScaler: A Collaborative Framework for Robust Autoscaling in the Cloud", PVLDB 17(12), 2024
Method: Collaborative predictive and reactive control with robustness margin
Limitation: Horizontal replica scaling on live services; no static per-VM recommendation and no held-out replay protocol

Paper: Zhou, Zhang, Delimitrou, "AQUATOPE: QoS-and-Uncertainty-Aware Resource Management for Multi-stage Serverless Workflows", ACM ASPLOS 2023
Method: Hybrid Bayesian neural networks for pre-warming and function-granularity allocation
Metric: QoS violation reduction (5x), cost reduction (34% avg)
Limitation: Sub-second serverless granularity; uncertainty model does not transfer to multi-day VM windows; single-point rather than a frontier

Paper: Qiu et al., "AWARE: Automate Workload Autoscaling with Reinforcement Learning in Production Cloud Systems", USENIX ATC 2023, pp. 315-330
Method: RL autoscaling with safe online training and offline pre-training
Metric: SLO violation rate, adaptation time, resource efficiency
Limitation: Learns a policy rather than exposing a decision surface; safety is a training constraint, not a reported quantity

Paper: Zhang et al., "AAPA: An Archetype-Aware Predictive Autoscaler with Uncertainty Quantification for Serverless Workloads on Kubernetes", arXiv:2507.05653, 2025 [preprint]
Method: Workload archetype clustering + uncertainty-quantified predictive autoscaling
Limitation: Interval coverage substitutes for realised violations; archetypes not tied to capacity-reclamation accounting

Paper: BACC: Budget-Aware Calibration and Control for Horizontal Autoscaling, arXiv:2606.20575, 2026 [preprint]
Method: Adaptive conformal inference as online calibration layer + budget-aware control setting aggressiveness
Limitation: Targets coverage for horizontal scaling, not per-VM flavour selection; reports no measured exhaustion frontier

Paper: Pozdniakova, Mazeika, Cholomskis, "SLA-Adaptive Threshold Adjustment for a Kubernetes Horizontal Pod Autoscaler", Electronics 13(7):1242, 2024
Method: EDA with moving-average smoothing to identify HPA target utilisation threshold
Metric: SLO-violating event count; SLO accuracy 1-2%; overprovisioning 4-10%
Limitation: Searches for the single best threshold rather than exposing the savings-vs-risk curve; operator receives one answer, not a choice

Paper: Luo et al., "Erms: Efficient Resource Management for Shared Microservices with SLA Guarantees", ACM ASPLOS 2023, pp. 62-77
Method: Latency-target decomposition and resource management under SLA constraints
Dataset / Testbed: Microservice benchmarks on a real cluster
Limitation: SLA enforced by admission and scheduling rather than predicted per-entity; no probability attached to an individual sizing decision

Paper: Ambati et al., "Providing SLOs for Resource-Harvesting VMs in Cloud Platforms", USENIX OSDI 2020, pp. 735-751 [pre-2021 anchor]
Method: Harvest VMs over spare capacity under explicit eviction and SLO contract
Limitation: Harvests spare platform cores rather than shrinking a tenant's own allocation; risk borne by the harvester, not the workload owner

Paper: Rzadca et al., "Autopilot: Workload Autoscaling at Google", EuroSys 2020, pp. 1-16 [pre-2021 anchor]
Method: Sliding-window and ML-based vertical autoscaling of container limits in production
Limitation: Reports slack and OOM rate as separate outcomes of one tuned policy, never as a frontier the operator traverses
